draft.title: Human-centred and earth-centred views
card: A world view is the set of beliefs a person or group holds about how the world works and what matters in it. It shapes how they see nature.
nature is valued for what it gives people, such as timber, water, food and space to build. People are seen as separate from nature and able to use it.
nature is valued for its own sake, whether or not it is useful to people. People are seen as one part of nature, not above it.
Most people hold a mix of views, and a person can value nature in both ways. The two views describe different starting points, not two fixed groups of people.
draft.remember: Human-centred: nature is valued for its use to people. Earth-centred: nature has worth in itself and people belong to it.

a.q: Which view of a wetland is earth-centred?
opts: A wetland deserves protection because it has its own worth
A wetland should be protected because it cleans our water
A wetland should be drained to make room for new farms
A wetland is useful because tourists pay to visit it
a.why: An earth-centred view values nature for its own sake, not for what it gives people. The water-cleaning option is tempting, but it values the wetland for its benefit to people, which is human-centred.
a.clue: Which reason would still hold if the place were of no use to people?

b.q: A council in Victoria's Otway Ranges wants to protect a patch of old forest. Which reason for protecting it is human-centred?
opts: The forest will attract walkers and bring money to the town
The trees and animals have a right to exist for themselves
People are one part of the forest, just like the animals
The forest has worth whether or not anyone ever visits it
b.why: Protecting the forest for the money walkers bring values it for what it gives people, so it is human-centred. The other options value the forest for itself or see people as part of it, which is earth-centred. Protecting nature does not make a view earth-centred: the reason matters.
b.clue: The action is the same in every option, so look at the reason given.

a.best: A wetland deserves protection because it has its own worth

b.best: The forest will attract walkers and bring money to the town
